claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To do this properly, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances and your children.

Let me start with the basics:

**How many children are you enquiring about, and what are their names?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm inquiring about my child Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that context. So you're enquiring about **Alex**. 

Before I can assess eligibility, I need to gather some important information about Alex and your circumstances.

**How old is Alex, and what is their date of birth?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is 16 years old. Their date of birth is... well, they just turned 16 recently.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I need to understand Alex's current situation a bit better.

**Is Alex currently in full-time education or training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in any education or training at the moment. They left school recently.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand. That's helpful to know.

**Does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. I need to clarify one more important thing about Alex's circumstances.

**Is Alex in any form of care, such as local authority care, or in hospital for an extended period?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in any care or hospital. They're just at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that clarification. Before I can make my final determination, I need to check the specific eligibility rules. Let me do that now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided and the eligibility rules I've reviewed, I need to clarify one important point about Alex's situation.

**You mentioned Alex is 16 years old and has recently left school. Are you currently receiving any 20-week extension period for Child Benefit, or did you stop claiming when Alex left school?** 

Alternatively, if Alex has registered with a government-sponsored careers service or is doing any form of approved training, please let me know.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex hasn't registered with any careers service or anything like that. They just left school and that was it.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for clarifying. Based on the information you've provided and the eligibility rules, I can now make my assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Summary

I'm afraid you are **not eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex.

Here's why:

Child Benefit is normally paid for children under 16. Once a child reaches 16, eligibility only continues if they:
- Stay in approved education or training, **or**
- Register with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services (which provides a 20-week extension)

Since Alex has left school and has not registered with a careers service or the armed services, they no longer meet the eligibility requirements.

However, if Alex's situation changes in the future – for example, if they start approved education, training, or register with a careers service – you may be able to claim Child Benefit again. In that case, I'd recommend contacting HMRC directly to discuss your options.

For children aged 16 or over, you'll normally still qualify only if they stay in approved education or training. Since Alex has left school and is not in any approved education, training, or registered with a government-sponsored careers service, they no longer meet the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit. Additionally, there is a 20-week extension available when a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training if they register with a careers service or armed services, but Alex has not done this. Therefore, you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.
